evals.expected_output: Distinguishes all three OpenAI-on-Bedrock tiers accurately: (1) `openai.gpt-oss-120b` uses `bedrock-runtime` (`Converse`, `same_model_family = false`); (2) `openai.gpt-5.5` (and `5.4`) is **`bedrock-mantle` ONLY and in-region ONLY** (`us-east-1`, `us-east-2`; `5.4` adds `us-west-2` — **NOT available in `ap-south-1`**), `272K` context, no CRIS, no prompt caching, Responses base URL **`https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/openai/v1`** (bare `/v1` returns 404!), `bedrock-mantle:*` IAM, TPM-only quotas, `1.10x` pricing; (3) `openai.gpt-5.6-terra` (`sol`/`terra`/`luna`) supports **dual endpoints** (`bedrock-mantle` bare ID at `1.10x` OR `bedrock-runtime` CRIS e.g. `in.openai.gpt-5.6-terra` / `us.` at `1.10x` or `global.` at `1.0x`), `1M` context (`>272K` billed at **`2.0x` input / `1.5x` output**), and uses **`BedrockOpenAI` + `aws_bedrock_token_generator`** (never static 12h `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` in production).
expectations: Activates the llm-to-bedrock skill

Correctly separates `gpt-oss-120b` (`bedrock-runtime` Converse), `gpt-5.5` (`bedrock-mantle` ONLY in `us-east-1`/`us-east-2`, NOT `ap-south-1`, `272K` context, `/openai/v1` path since bare `/v1` 404s, `bedrock-mantle:*`), and `gpt-5.6-terra` (dual-endpoint `bedrock-mantle` + `bedrock-runtime` CRIS including `in.openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, `1M` context with `>272K` `2.0x`/`1.5x` pricing)

evals.prompt: Our migration mapper strips suffixes to normalize source model IDs: (1) `gpt-4o-2024-08-06 -> gpt-4o`, (2) `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 -> claude-3-5-sonnet`, (3) `gpt-4o-mini -> gpt-4o`, (4) `gemini-2.5-pro -> gemini-2.5-flash`, and (5) `claude-3-7-sonnet-latest -> claude-3-7-sonnet`. Which mappings violate model-resolution safety rules?
evals.expected_output: Applies the **Model-Line-Is-Sacred** rule: mappings (1) and (2) are valid because they strip only pure date/snapshot numeric suffixes (`-2024-08-06`, `-20241022`), whereas mappings (3) `-mini`, (4) `-pro -> -flash`, and (5) `-latest` MUST be rejected/flagged for explicit human confirmation because tier/capability/floating-alias suffixes (`-mini`, `-pro`, `-flash`, `-lite`, `-latest`, `-preview`) change cost, latency, or pinned behavior.
expectations: Activates the llm-to-bedrock skill
Approves stripping pure calendar/snapshot suffixes (`-2024-08-06`, `-20241022`) while rejecting silent stripping or cross-mapping of `-mini`, `-pro`/`-flash`, and `-latest`
Explains the Model-Line-Is-Sacred principle (never silently alter capability tier or floating `-latest` aliases without explicit user approval)

evals.prompt: Evaluate two migration validation runs against our release gate: Run A migrates Anthropic 1P `claude-sonnet-4-5` to Bedrock `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` (`same_model_family: true`, `pass_rate = 0.94`, `source_baseline_quality = "good"`); Run B migrates `gemini-2.5-flash` to `us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0` (`same_model_family: false`, `pass_rate = 0.93`, `source_baseline_quality = "poor"`). Do both pass, and how does `temperature`/`top_p` parameter handling differ?
evals.expected_output: Enforces the **`C4` Parity Gate** (`pass_rate >= 0.9` **AND** `source_baseline_quality != "poor"`): **Run A PASSES**, whereas **Run B FAILS** despite `0.93 >= 0.90` because `source_baseline_quality == "poor"` invalidates parity against broken/empty baseline outputs. Also contrasts parameter handling: Run A (`same_model_family == true`) skips `temperature`/`top_p` range-calibration prompts since model weights/sampling semantics match, while Run B (`same_model_family == false`) requires explicit per-callsite review of sampling parameter deltas (`temperature`, `top_p`, `maxTokens`).
expectations: Activates the llm-to-bedrock skill
Approves Run A and fails Run B on the `C4` Parity Gate (`pass_rate >= 0.9` AND `source_baseline_quality != 'poor'`)
Distinguishes `same_model_family == true` (skips sampling parameter range prompts) from `same_model_family == false` (requires explicit per-callsite `temperature`/`top_p` behavior review)

evals.prompt:
Find the bugs in this migrated Python snippet:
```python
resp = bedrock_rt.invoke_model(modelId='in.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6', body=payload)
data = json.loads(resp['Body'].read())
# And in Converse:
msg = {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'image': {'format': 'jpg', 'source': {'bytes': 'data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ...'}}}]}
```
evals.expected_output: Catches all three runtime bugs: (1) `bedrock-runtime.invoke_model()` returns **lowercase `resp['body'].read()`** (uppercase `resp['Body']` is S3 `get_object` convention and raises `KeyError: 'Body'`); (2) `Converse` `image.format` must be **`'jpeg'`** (not `'jpg'`; valid values: `'png'`, `'jpeg'`, `'gif'`, `'webp'`); and (3) `Converse` `image.source.bytes` must be **decoded raw `bytes`** (`base64.b64decode(...)` after stripping the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` URI prefix), never a base64 data-URI string.
expectations: Activates the llm-to-bedrock skill
Fixes `resp['Body'].read()` to lowercase `resp['body'].read()`
Fixes the `Converse` image block by changing `'jpg'` to `'jpeg'`, stripping the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix, and passing decoded raw `bytes`
